canonicalName: Optimal transport and synthetic Ricci curvature

milestones.label: Polar factorization through optimal transport
milestones.work: Y. Brenier, Polar factorization and monotone rearrangement of vector-valued functions, CPAM 44 (1991)
milestones.description: Brenier established polar factorization using a Monge–Kantorovich problem, a precursor to the later metric-measure curvature definitions.

evidence.claim: Publisher gives June 1991 and describes the Monge–Kantorovich method.

milestones.label: Ricci bounds defined through optimal transport
milestones.work: J. Lott and C. Villani, Ricci curvature for metric-measure spaces via optimal transport, arXiv:math/0412127 (2004)
milestones.description: The public preprint defines synthetic lower Ricci curvature bounds for measured length spaces via displacement convexity.

evidence.claim: ArXiv records the December 2004 public submission and states the definition in the abstract.

milestones.note: Sturm developed a closely related formulation; priority and comparison need separate review.

works.citation: Ricci curvature for metric-measure spaces via optimal transport

notes: The 2004 arXiv submission predates the 2009 journal issue. Sturm’s independent curvature-dimension work and the first purposeful application still need adjudication; no naming institution verified.

milestones.label: Counting rational points on definable sets
milestones.work: J. Pila and A. J. Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke Math. J. 133 (2006)
milestones.description: The counting theorem supplies the rational-point bound later used in diophantine applications.

evidence.claim: Publisher record identifies the 2006 Pila–Wilkie paper.

milestones.label: Counting method applied to Manin–Mumford
milestones.work: J. Pila and U. Zannier, Rational points in periodic analytic sets and the Manin-Mumford conjecture, arXiv:0802.4016 (2008)
milestones.description: Pila and Zannier explicitly combine rational-point upper bounds with torsion-point lower bounds to reprove Manin–Mumford.

evidence.claim: The 2008 abstract states the target theorem and counting method.

works.citation: The rational points of a definable set
works.whyItMatters: Developed the counting theorem and its diophantine use

notes: The earliest public statement of the full o-minimal diophantine programme, later André–Oort milestones and a naming institution remain open.

canonicalName: Periodic torus orbits, subconvexity and homogeneous dynamics

milestones.label: Periodic torus orbit distribution studied
milestones.work: M. Einsiedler, E. Lindenstrauss, P. Michel and A. Venkatesh, The distribution of periodic torus orbits on homogeneous spaces, arXiv:math/0607815 (2006)
milestones.description: The preprint studies equidistribution of periodic torus orbits using orbit separation and measure rigidity.

evidence.claim: ArXiv records the 2006 public preprint and its methods.

milestones.label: Cubic-field analogue of Duke’s theorem
milestones.work: M. Einsiedler et al., Distribution of periodic torus orbits and Duke’s theorem for cubic fields, arXiv:0708.1113 (2007)
milestones.description: The follow-up applies subconvexity and measure classification to equidistribution for cubic fields.

evidence.claim: The 2007 abstract identifies the cubic-field result and techniques.

works.citation: The distribution of periodic torus orbits on homogeneous spaces

notes: These dates use public arXiv submissions rather than the 2009 journal issue. Earlier precursors and a named institution remain to be checked.

milestones.label: Weil–Petersson volume recursion published online
milestones.work: M. Mirzakhani, Simple geodesics and Weil–Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, Invent. Math. 167 (2007)
milestones.description: The published work relates simple geodesics and Weil–Petersson volumes of moduli spaces.

evidence.claim: Publisher metadata dates the online publication to 12 October 2006; the bound volume is dated 2007.

works.citation: Simple geodesics and Weil–Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces

notes: The publisher dates online publication to 12 October 2006, although the bound Inventiones volume is 2007. Mirzakhani’s 2004 Harvard thesis may contain the earlier public formulation; its availability and date must be checked before assigning first_statement. First application and named institution remain open.

milestones.label: Conformal invariance of triangular-lattice percolation
milestones.work: S. Smirnov, Critical percolation in the plane: conformal invariance, Cardy’s formula, scaling limits, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 333 (2001)
milestones.description: The published paper establishes Cardy’s formula and conformal invariance for critical site percolation on the triangular lattice.

evidence.claim: Publisher record dates the paper to August 2001 and states its result.

milestones.label: Holomorphic fermions in the Ising model
milestones.work: S. Smirnov, Conformal invariance in random cluster models. I. Holomorphic fermions in the Ising model, arXiv:0708.0039 (2007)
milestones.description: The public preprint constructs discrete holomorphic observables for the critical Ising model.

evidence.claim: ArXiv records the 2007 preprint and describes the Ising construction.

works.citation: Critical percolation in the plane: conformal invariance, Cardy’s formula, scaling limits

notes: The 2001 percolation paper precedes the 2007 Ising preprint; its final journal version is later. The first purposeful use as a tool and named institution remain open.

milestones.label: Low-influence invariance principle stated
milestones.work: E. Mossel, R. O’Donnell and K. Oleszkiewicz, Noise stability of functions with low influences: invariance and optimality, arXiv:math/0503503 (2005)
milestones.description: The public preprint proves an invariance principle for low-influence multilinear polynomials.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public submission to 2005 and states the principle.

milestones.note: This is the first public statement of this specific invariance principle, not of Boolean-function analysis generally.

milestones.label: Majority Is Stablest proved
milestones.work: E. Mossel, R. O’Donnell and K. Oleszkiewicz, Noise stability of functions with low influences, arXiv:math/0503503 (2005)
milestones.description: The same preprint applies the invariance principle to the Majority Is Stablest conjecture.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly names the application.

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both roles.

works.citation: Noise stability of functions with low influences: invariance and optimality
works.whyItMatters: Co-proved the invariance principle and its application

notes: The 2005 public preprint predates its 2010 Annals issue. Other founders and institutional naming for Boolean-function analysis remain to be researched.

milestones.label: Dense graph limit object described
milestones.work: L. Lovász and B. Szegedy, Limits of dense graph sequences, arXiv:math/0408173 (2004)
milestones.description: The preprint represents limits of convergent dense-graph sequences by symmetric measurable functions.

evidence.claim: ArXiv records the 2004 public preprint and describes the limit object.

milestones.label: Graph-limit monograph published
milestones.work: L. Lovász, Large Networks and Graph Limits, AMS Colloquium Publications 60 (2012)
milestones.description: The monograph systematically presents graph limits and their applications.

evidence.claim: AMS bibliographic record identifies the 2012 monograph.

notes: The 2004 preprint predates the 2006 journal issue. Earliest use of the word graphon in a title and first institutional recognition remain unverified.

milestones.label: Differential privacy formally defined
milestones.work: C. Dwork, F. McSherry, K. Nissim and A. Smith, Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity in Private Data Analysis, TCC (2006)
milestones.description: The conference paper characterizes privacy via transcript indistinguishability and calibrates noise to query sensitivity.

evidence.claim: Publisher dates the paper to 2006 and its abstract states the definition and mechanism.

milestones.label: Algorithmic foundations monograph
milestones.work: C. Dwork and A. Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy, Foundations and Trends in TCS 9 (2014)
milestones.description: A monograph systematizes differential-privacy algorithms and theory.

works.citation: Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity in Private Data Analysis
works.whyItMatters: Co-defined differential privacy and sensitivity-calibrated noise

notes: Harvard’s publication list confirms Dwork’s 2006 ICALP paper titled Differential Privacy; its order relative to TCC and any earlier public version needs a separate priority check. The first real-world application is not assigned.

milestones.label: Sparse recovery from incomplete Fourier samples
milestones.work: E. Candès, J. Romberg and T. Tao, Robust Uncertainty Principles: Exact Signal Reconstruction from Highly Incomplete Frequency Information, arXiv:math/0409186 (2004)
milestones.description: The preprint proves sparse-signal recovery from incomplete frequency information using convex minimization.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public submission to September 2004 and describes the recovery theorem.

milestones.note: This is a foundational public result; other 2004 precursors still require priority comparison.

milestones.label: Compressed sensing paper published
milestones.work: D. Donoho, Compressed Sensing, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 52 (2006)
milestones.description: Donoho’s named treatment helped define the compressed-sensing programme.

works.citation: Robust Uncertainty Principles: Exact Signal Reconstruction from Highly Incomplete Frequency Information

notes: The catalogue’s 2006 journal dates conceal the 2004 public preprint. The first title containing “compressed sensing,” first practical application and institutional date still need verification.

canonicalName: Gauge-theory heuristics for rational points (non-abelian Chabauty)

milestones.label: Unipotent Albanese and Selmer-variety approach
milestones.work: M. Kim, The unipotent Albanese map and Selmer varieties for curves, arXiv:math/0510441 (2005)
milestones.description: The public preprint relates p-adic path torsors and Selmer varieties to Diophantine finiteness questions.

evidence.claim: ArXiv records the 2005 public submission and its abstract states the construction.

milestones.note: The journal version appeared in 2009; this role is scoped to Kim’s approach, not all nonabelian Diophantine methods.

works.citation: The unipotent Albanese map and Selmer varieties for curves

notes: The 2009 publisher record confirms the journal version and submission in 2007, while arXiv has the earlier 2005 public version. Grothendieck’s 1983 private letter is a precursor, not a public conceptual date. First successful target application remains to be pinned down.
